applicability: Applies to counting distinct primes formable from permutations of up to max_length distinct digits drawn from a supplied set of distinct decimal digits 0-9, with no leading zero for multi-digit numbers. Requires max_length between 1 and 4 and not exceeding the number of supplied digits. Rejects malformed inputs, duplicate or out-of-range digits, booleans, and unsupported max_length values via ValueError.
description: Exhaustively generate every ordered selection of k distinct digits for k from 1 through max_length, skip multi-digit sequences with a leading zero, convert each to an integer, and test primality exactly by trial division using the 6k±1 optimization after handling small cases. Primes are accumulated in a set so each distinct prime is counted once; the answer is the set size. The search space is tiny (at most a few thousand permutations), so the method is complete and deterministic. Uncertainty is minimal; the only assumptions are the stated domain constraints (distinct digits 0-9, max_length 1-4, max_length not exceeding the digit count).
